stories.title: Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has signed Madewell to a long-term lease for 7,340 square feet at 1 Rockefeller Plaza. Slated to open in 2027, the new store marks Madewell’s first location at Rockefeller Center. Madewell offers premium denim, apparel, and accessories for women and men. Best known for its denim expertise, the brand is recognized for its thoughtful design, innovative approach to denim, and everyday wardrobe essential. The new store will bring the full Madewell experience to life, showcasing the brand’s denim expertise, signature styling, and community-focused programming, according to Tishman Speyer. “Rockefeller Center continues to attract brands that shape culture and consumer behavior globally,” said EB Kelly, Senior Managing Director at Tishman Speyer and Head of Rockefeller Center. “Madewell’s decision to establish a presence here reinforces the Center’s unique ability to combine iconic New York identity with modern cultural relevance.” The post Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Madewell signs 7,340 sq ft lease at 1 Rockefeller Plaza, opening 2027.
Retail tenant commitment reinforces Manhattan's flagship mixed-use asset strength.
Minimal direct multifamily impact; office/retail news, not residential demand signal.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer has leased space to Madewell at Rockefeller Center, with the apparel retailer slated to open its first location there in 2027. The 7,340-square-foot store will showcase the brand's full experience and programming. The lease reflects continued tenant confidence in Rockefeller Center's iconic Manhattan location and cultural draw.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is a retail/office transaction that signals health in Manhattan's mixed-use flagship market but does not directly inform apartment demand, supply, or feasibility metrics.

stories.title: NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial has listed 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District for sale, presenting an owner-user opportunity encompassing approximately 99,280 square feet across eight stories. Executive managing director Ryan Campbell, SIOR, and EVP Scott Martin are representing the property. Built in 1924 and currently vacant, 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. features a marble-tile lobby, three Otis traction elevators, including two passenger elevators and one freight elevator, and approximately 300 tons of water-cooled chiller capacity. The building also features emergency power supported by two Generac diesel generators and a fully addressable fire alarm and sprinkler system. “530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. represents a rare opportunity for an owner-user to acquire a substantial office building in one of Pasadena’s most walkable and amenity-rich districts,” said campbell. “The combination of scale, parking, transit access and a central Colorado Boulevard location gives an owner the ability to establish a significant long-term presence in Pasadena while taking advantage of a market where owner-user acquisitions have already reduced available office inventory.” The post NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd., Pasadena: 99,280 sq ft, 8-story vacant office, listed for owner-user.
Owner-user sales reducing available office inventory in walkable Pasadena district.
Weak office demand; no direct multifamily signal but reflects broader Los Angeles office oversupply.
stories.summary: NAI Capital is marketing 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd., a vacant 99,280-square-foot office building built in 1924, as an owner-user opportunity in Pasadena's Playhouse Village District. The eight-story asset features updated systems, parking, and transit access. The broker noted that owner-user acquisitions have already reduced available office inventory in the area.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, the shift toward owner-user conversions and reduced office absorption in Pasadena's walkable urban core may eventually free capital and attention for mixed-use or residential redevelopment if office vacancy persists in the Los Angeles metro.

stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. (01:04) Retail’s Demand Visibility Problem (02:44) Why Sytes (04:04) A Filtration System for Tenant Demand (06:24) Getting First Customers to Pay Upfront (07:24) Why Tenant Demand Data Was Opaque (08:34) Anonymous Tenant Expansion (10:14) How a Deal Happens on Sytes (11:24) Church’s Chicken Case Study (14:54) Kimco & MyEyeDoctor Portfolio Review (16:34) REITs & Strip Centers (18:04) The Subscription Model (19:24) Retail Is Back (22:44) AI Leasing Agents & the Broker’s Future (24:04) Tenant Demand Index for Developers (27:24) Bootstrapping vs. Venture Capital Backing (28:24) Collaboration Superpower: Travis Kalanick Learn more: –Visit Sytes –Rafael Weiss on LinkedIn Virtual Events: –AI & Innovation Forum: Multifamily: on 9/29 –SFR / BTR Forum: on 10/22 In-person Events: –Institutional Investors & PE Forum: in NYC on 9/16 –South Florida Capital & Development Forum: in Miami on 10/15 –Finance Forum: in NYC on 11/3 –All upcoming Commercial Observer events Connect with Tangent: -Edward Cohen on LinkedIn -Zach Aarons on LinkedIn -Tangent on LinkedIn
bullets: Sytes platform connects 350+ tenants, 35,000+ retail listings across 50 states.
Addresses retail tenant demand visibility; serves Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, Dutch Bros.
Retail tech tool; no direct multifamily application or demand/supply signal.
stories.summary: Sytes is a marketplace platform co-founded by Rafael Weiss that matches commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively seeking space in real time. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with major clients including Kimco and InvenTrust. The podcast discusses how Sytes solves retail leasing information asymmetry and uses tenant demand data to inform deal flow.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. Sytes focuses on retail and commercial leasing transparency; multifamily has distinct leasing systems and tenant acquisition channels (corporate vs. individual household renters).

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management buys 2 affordable housing properties: $115.4M, 570 units total.
Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) + Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M) in Miami-Dade Little River.
Freddie Mac financing backing acquisitions; institutional capital active in workforce housing.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management has acquired two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, bringing total recent investment to $115.4 million across 570 units. The acquisitions include Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M) in Little River. Both deals were financed by CBRE Capital Markets with Freddie Mac-backed loans at favorable terms.
stories.impact: Signals sustained institutional appetite for workforce/affordable multifamily in Miami-Dade despite broader market tightness. Freddie Mac's active participation and favorable loan terms (interest-only, minimal escrows) suggest GSE confidence in Miami affordable housing fundamentals. Competition for stabilized workforce assets in Miami-Dade is intensifying, potentially raising acquisition prices for similar-profile deals and limiting development feasibility for new-build workforce product without subsidy.

stories.title: Joint Venture Tops Off Construction on Mount Vernon Workforce Housing
stories.excerpt: City, county and state officials joined together to celebrate the topping off of QWest Towers, a new $158-million workforce housing development that is nearing completion in Mount Vernon, NY. Located at 1 and 25 North MacQuesten Pkwy., the project is being developed by QWest Towers LLC, a joint venture between Simone Development Companies and Stagg Group, in collaboration with the Rev. Dr. L’Judie Matt-Simmons. The 228-unit project consists of a 15-story tower and 12-story tower. The first tower will be completed later this year, with the second one to follow within a few months. Construction financing for the project includes support from New York State Housing and Community Renewal, Westchester County’s New Homes Land Acquisition program and the county’s Housing Flex Fund. The project also received financial incentives from the Mount Vernon Industrial Development Agency. ool District and the Mount Vernon Fire Department. stories.summary: A joint venture between Simone Development Companies and Stagg Group is completing QWest Towers, a $158 million, 228-unit workforce housing project in Mount Vernon, NY. The development consists of two towers (15 and 12 stories) at 1 and 25 North MacQuesten Parkway. The first tower will deliver later this year, with the second following within months. Construction was supported by New York State Housing and Community Renewal, Westchester County's New Homes Land Acquisition program, and local IDA incentives.
stories.impact: Supply addition to Westchester County rental market signals state and county commitment to workforce housing entitlements and financing programs. Completion of 228 units in Mount Vernon may moderate rent growth in the Westchester corridor if absorption is slow, but also validates development feasibility for similar-profile suburban workforce projects with public financing support. Developers targeting Westchester should track Mt. Vernon lease-up velocity and pricing to calibrate underwriting for competing projects.

stories.title: Javits Center Expansion, Tech Upgrades Boosting NYC Hospitality Industry
stories.excerpt: Five years after the Javits Center underwent a $1.5 billion expansion, the Hudson Yards convention venue is continuing to expand its bandwidth to boost its events business and the adjacent New York City hospitality industry. The 3.3 million-square-foot facility recently underwent a $5 million technology upgrade enabling the Javits Center to become the first convention center in the U.S. to provide the newest wireless network, Wi-Fi 7, Commercial Observer can first report. The Wi-Fi 7 system, which debuted last month for Fanatics Fest, provides another competitive edge in attracting more conferences and events going forward, Joyce Leveston, CEO of the Javits Center, told CO. The original Jacob Javits Center opened in 1986. PHOTO: Edmund Vincent Gillon/Museum of the City of New York/Getty Images “So many people who are coming to conventions also want to feel that they can remotely connect with their workplace,” Leveston said on Wednesday, moments before the Javits Center marked its 40th anniversary with a celebration event. “You can’t do that unless you have a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system.” The technology enhancement is just the latest effort by the Javits Center to up the ante in terms of drawing some of the biggest conferences and events to Manhattan and providing a jolt to New York City’s economy. The Javits Center estimates that its convention bookings generated more than 100,000 hotel stays in the New York City region in 2025. The expansion of the Javits Center, which debuted in May 2021, added 1.2 million square feet to the north side of the complex, including a 55,000-square-foot ballroom and a glass-enclosed sustainable rooftop pavilion touted as the largest green roof in the Northeast. The boost to New York City’s hospitality industry from new investments to the Javits Center is evident across the street at 418 11th Avenue, where a new 455-room Hilton-branded hotel is slated to open in the next three years as part of a larger mixed-use project. The expansion follows the facility's $1.5 billion renovation five years prior and underscores efforts to strengthen its competitive positioning.
stories.impact: Indirectly supportive of Manhattan multifamily demand. Javits Center capex spending on tech and events programming drives convention attendee volume and corporate travel to Hudson Yards and broader Manhattan. Increased event calendar density and hotel occupancy support labor in-migration, corporate relocations, and temporary-to-permanent housing conversion, boosting rental demand in western Midtown and Hudson Yards submarkets. Multifamily developers targeting Hudson Yards should monitor Javits event pipeline and hotel absorption rates as a leading indicator of housing demand.

stories.title: Westphal Company Lands $56M Refi for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Westphal Company has secured $56.1 million in permanent financing for a 354-unit apartment complex in eastern San Diego County. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate financing through the firm’s Fannie Mae platform. The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year term with interest-only payments for the full term. Property records identify Westphal Company owns the Wintercrest Village Apartments, a garden-style community at 12002 Wintercrest Drive in Lakeside, Calif., which is an unincorporated community roughly 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, along with two swimming pools and spas, outdoor courtyards, and fitness rooms. Northmarq’s Aaron Beck, Conor Freeman and Robbie Driscoll facilitated the financing, which allowed Westphal to extract equity from the property while maintaining its cash flow, according to Beck. The lender also waived all operating escrows. “With this Fannie Mae refinance, we were able to unlock trapped equity for the borrower and preserve cash flow while keeping the loan truly non-recourse with no carve-out guarantees,” Beck said in a statement. San Diego’s multifamily market stabilized in the second quarter, with vacancy holding at 5 percent and asking rents rising 0.5 percent to $2,598 per month, according to Northmarq’s second-quarter data. Investment sales slowed roughly 25 percent compared to last year, but median pricing jumped 25 percent to $415,000 per unit. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Westphal Company refinances Wintercrest Village Apartments, Lakeside CA: $56.1M, 354 units.
Fannie Mae fixed-rate, 10-year, interest-only; no operating escrows; equity extraction preserved.
San Diego County suburban market showing refinance liquidity; stabilized garden-style product in demand.
stories.summary: Westphal Company secured $56.1 million in permanent Fannie Mae financing for Wintercrest Village Apartments, a 354-unit garden-style complex in Lakeside, CA (20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego). The nonrecourse loan carries a fixed rate, 10-year term, interest-only payments, and no operating escrows. The refinance allowed Westphal to unlock trapped equity while preserving cash flow.
stories.impact: Signals strong Fannie Mae appetite for suburban San Diego multifamily and favorable lending terms for stabilized assets. Garden-style product in eastern San Diego County (lower-cost submarket) remains financeable even with interest-rate environment; equity availability for stable operators suggests healthy NOI and cap-rate compression in the Lakeside/unincorporated area. Developers targeting San Diego suburbs should note Fannie Mae's active positioning and be prepared for continued refinance competition; persistent liquidity may suppress new development feasibility if cap rates compress further.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinances Design Center of Americas, Dania Beach FL: $45M loan.
780,000 sq ft office/design showroom; $3M invested since 2024 credit bid, $3–5M planned.

stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, FL, securing a $45 million loan from City National Bank of Florida. Fortress acquired the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex through a $76 million credit bid in 2024 after a foreclosure battle with previous owner Charles Cohen. The firm has invested $3 million in updates and plans $3–5 million more in renovations over the next year.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. This is an office/design showroom recovery play; Fortress's refinance signals some stabilization in South Florida commercial real estate post-distress, but the asset class (office/showroom) and loss of major tenant Chewy (100,000 sq ft to Plantation Pointe) reflect broader South Florida office headwinds. No demand or supply signal for multifamily; however, Fortress's capital deployment in commercial distressed assets may indicate selective opportunism in South Florida CRE—developers should monitor for potential mixed-use or conversion plays if Design Center fundamentals continue to decline.
